newsitem.title: USA: BankBoston says it ends sale of finance unit to Mercury.
newsitem.headline: BankBoston says it ends sale of finance unit to Mercury.

text.p: BankBoston Corp. said Thursday it was ending an agreement to sell its Fidelity Acceptance Corp. finance unit to Mercury Finance Co. because of financial problems at Mercury.

BankBoston said in a brief statement that it regarded the events at Mercury as a breach of the agreement announced on Jan. 10 that called for Mercury to issue stock to BankBoston for Fidelity. Lake Forest, Ill.-based Mercury, an auto-loan company, said Wednesday that phony bookkeeping entries had inflated its earnings and that it fired its chief accountant.

"BankBoston today informed Mercury Finance Co. that recent events regarding Mercury Finance constituted a breach of the provisions of BankBoston's agreement for the exchange of shares of Fidelity Acceptance Corp. for shares of Mercury Finance. As a result, BankBoston has sent notice of breach and termination of the agreement to Mercury Finance," the company said.

Mercury Finance said Wednesday that it found problems in its bookkeeping that caused it to overstate earnings by $90 million over four years and that its chief accountant, who had apparently disappeared, had been fired.
BankBoston's agreement called for Mercury to issue 32.7 million common shares to BankBoston for Fidelity. When the deal was announced on Jan. 10, the stock was worth about $458 million.

Mercury Finance stock has not traded since it closed at $14.875 on the New York Stock Exchange on Tuesday. The NYSE would not indicate where the stock might open but traders said it was changing hands at $4.25 overseas. That would make the 32.7 million shares worth about $139 million.
